files.description: Clinic appointments in New York (160 rows, February to November 2025, so the clock changes in March and November fall inside the data): appt_id (whole number), local_start (New York wall-clock start, text YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, no UTC offset), start_with_offset (the same moment as ISO text with its UTC offset, e.g. "2025-06-13T08:45:00-04:00"), clinic (Harbor, Midtown or Riverside; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty).

task_text: Every appointment gets a follow-up visit four weeks later at the same New York wall-clock time (local_start is New York local time). `result` should be a table with the columns appt_id and follow_up_utc, the follow-up time converted to UTC and written as text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM', in file order.
intended_computation: Add 28 calendar days to each New York wall-clock start (160 appointments), localise to New York and convert to UTC, written as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'.

predicted_direction.reason: with the 2.x time-zone library adding weeks to a stdlib datetime keeps the old offset, so UTC is off by one hour across the clock change

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
